Inclusion: approved by the LSC (2017), installed (2018) and operating, with published detector, background and performance results. No WIMP exclusion limit from TREX-DM data was found in any source read, so tier C.
Surface phase: the detector was operated at the Universidad de Zaragoza as a proof of concept before the move (arXiv:1812.04519, arXiv:1509.02035); that surface laboratory is not an Atlas site.

summary.plain: TREX-DM looks for very light dark matter particles with a high-pressure gas chamber read out by Micromegas detectors, installed at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees. Light gases (neon or argon) make the tiny recoils detectable. Its published results so far describe detector performance and background levels.
summary.technical: TPC Rare Event eXperiment for Dark Matter: a 20 L gas TPC (up to 10 bar; 0.30 kg Ar or 0.16 kg Ne) with two side-by-side modules read by 25x25 cm^2 microbulk Micromegas planes (about 1000 channels), shielded by 5 cm of copper, 20 cm of lead and 40 cm of neutron moderator. Installed in Hall A of the LSC (2450 m.w.e.) in 2018, run with Ne + 2% isobutane at 4 bar in 2019-2022 (background 80 counts/keV/kg/day at 1-7 keVee after a radon fix, threshold 1 keVee), re-installed in Lab2500 in 2023.
